newsitem.title: CANADA: Ontario regulator to review electronic trading.
newsitem.headline: Ontario regulator to review electronic trading.

text.p: The Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) said on Friday that it was reviewing the market effects of electronic trading systems that were not sponsored by self-regulatory organizations (SROs) such as stock exchanges or Canada's Investment Dealers Association.

The OSC said non-SRO sponsored electronic trading systems or NETS are computer screen-based systems that automate order handling within a brokerage firm, route stock orders from a brokerage firm to a stock exchange, or take the place of a stock exchange trading floor.

The OSC said it was accepting written submissions to the Requests for Comments section of its weekly "OSC Bulletin" newsletter and would hold a public meeting in September 1997 to discuss the implications of market fragmentation due to NETS and the development of a regulatory model to govern them.

The OSC said the discussion would include the causes and implications of market fragmentation, the basis on which NETS should be permitted to operate in Canadian securities markets and proposals for new regulations and the role of the Ontario Securities Commission.

The OSC said Canadian securities regulators had been engaged since 1988 in discussions about the appropriate role of NETS. In September 1995, Instinet Corp, a subsidiary of Reuters Holdings Plc, was granted registration as an international dealer, permitting it to provide terminals to Ontario Designated Institutions to trade foreign securities not listed on a Canadian stock exchange directly on the Instinet network.

In its decision, the Commission stated that "a process should be put in place through which the Commission could obtain meaningful data and input concerning the issue of fragmentation of the markets in Canada."

In January 1997, the Toronto Stock Exchange released the report of its Special Committee on Market Fragmentation, which made recommendations for specific trading rule changes aimed at reducing internal fragmentation.
The report also suggested some possible frameworks for permitting Proprietary Electronic Trading Systems in the Canadian securities markets.
The Toronto Stock Exchange is expected to hold a conference on equity market fragmentation on June 3 and 4, 1997 to consider related issues.
